images.title: Counting dots on sides
images.purpose: Show that on dot paper a tilted figure with equal dot counts on its sides has equal sides, and swapped counts give a right angle.
images.composition: A tilted square on a dot grid, with two sides showing staircases, wide margins.
images.exact_structure: A grid of dots. A tilted square with corners P, Q, R, S on dots: P at (0, 0), Q at (3, −2), R at (5, 1), S at (2, 3). Side PQ is 3 across and 2 down, shown as a staircase in teal #0072B2. Side QR is 2 across and 3 down, shown as a staircase in amber #E69F00. The other 2 sides are plain lines. A small right-angle sign at Q. Exactly 4 corners.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Equal dot counts mean equal sides, and swapped counts mean a right angle.
images.description: A tilted square with corners on dots; side PQ goes 3 across and 2 down, side QR goes 2 across and 3 down, with a right angle at Q.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the dots across and down on each marked side.

image_decisions.why: Dot counts on two sides carry the idea.
